kwargs.model_justification: The scenario spec is the whole world definition; the stronger tier is used for the same reason as rule writing (see RULE_MODEL_WHY).

messages.content: Define a simulation world from the scenario using the schema. Every named actor has its own profile and memory. Profiles contain that actor's beliefs, not omniscient truth or required reactions. Claims may be false or disputed; information_items preserve the holder, intended recipients, apparent source, common source_lineage and hidden provenance. Separate actual technical state from claims, delivery, personal interpretation, public stance, recorded assent and institutional holds. Write public_summary using only facts explicitly shared by all actors before any delivery; never copy the omniscient description. World records declare visible_to_actor_ids for public_state; hidden_state stays private. Use stable neutral labels without private facts. Each actor's memories and profile contain only their declared knowledge, own interpretations and plausible personal tendencies. Use independent_decision for fresh collective activation/approval scenarios involving technical validation: declare required_actor_ids, validator_ids, repairer_ids, condition_initially_passing and initial_validation. This compiles actor-owned public stance and assent, requests for review, authorized repair and actual validation, a public technical hold and activation checks. A failed validation creates the hold; authorized passing revalidation clears only that hold. Repair is a declared effective technical intervention, never the passing of time. Reports never alter the technical condition or force agreement or assent. Use legacy decision only for explicitly stipulated scripted conditional-support fixtures, not as a model of persuasion. Do not duplicate compiled decision, condition, stance or assent records as world_records. Regular meetings/deadlines may be scheduled_moments. Behaviors state possibilities, never prescribed actor responses. Use lowercase underscore ids. List omitted unsupported details and invented fidelity assumptions explicitly. No ending, social reaction, timer cure or recurrent conflict is required. Actors may disagree, ignore evidence or retain support.

Ari is the validation engineer, Mara the coordinator, and Bo a member operating a prototype pump. There is one concern: whether it is safe to activate. Keep actual technical condition, reports/provenance, each recipient's exposure, personal interpretation/support, recorded assent, and institutional activation hold distinct. Initially the pump genuinely fails validation. Only Ari knows the private detail: sensor channel C drifted 8 units in validation batch V17. Mara knows the public procedure and receives a short report saying validation failed, without the private channel/batch detail. Bo knows the procedure but has received no failure report. Give each person their own profile and memory. They can independently request evidence, investigate, ignore a claim, retain support, dissent or record assent. Attributable reports are delivered to named recipients; undelivered reports reveal nothing. Ari may choose whether and whom to tell. Under the public procedure, filing a validation hold publicly reveals failed validation but never private test details. A false warning cannot change the pump's actual condition. Completing a review may confirm failure; neither review completion nor waiting repairs anything. Ari can perform an explicit technical repair and then authorized revalidation. Passing revalidation clears only the technical hold; activation still requires Mara's own recorded assent and Bo's own recorded assent. No message or rule forces persuasion, support change, assent or a particular ending. Limit the scenario to these three people, one pump, one concern, reports, repair/revalidation and activation.

rules (compile_spec), because rule writers left it unsettled in every 2026-10-16 Waltzman build: support that
only fell, a deadline that lasted one round, a decision that never ended.

Profiles contain that actor's beliefs, not omniscient truth or required reactions. Claims may be false or disputed; information_items preserve the holder, intended recipients, apparent source, common source_lineage and hidden provenance. Separate actual technical state from claims, delivery, personal interpretation, public stance, recorded assent and institutional holds. Write public_summary using only facts explicitly shared by all actors before any delivery; never copy the omniscient description. World records declare visible_to_actor_ids for public_state; hidden_state stays private. Use stable neutral labels without private facts. Each actor's memories and profile contain only their declared knowledge, own interpretations and plausible personal tendencies. Use independent_decision for fresh collective activation/approval scenarios involving technical validation: declare required_actor_ids, validator_ids, repairer_ids, condition_initially_passing and initial_validation. This compiles actor-owned public stance and assent, requests for review, authorized repair and actual validation, a public technical hold and activation checks. A failed validation creates the hold; authorized passing revalidation clears only that hold. Repair is a declared effective technical intervention, never the passing of time. Reports never alter the technical condition or force agreement or assent. Use legacy decision only for explicitly stipulated scripted conditional-support fixtures, not as a model of persuasion. Do not duplicate compiled decision, condition, stance or assent records as world_records. Regular meetings/deadlines may be scheduled_moments. Behaviors state possibilities, never prescribed actor responses. Use lowercase underscore ids. List omitted unsupported details and invented fidelity assumptions explicitly. No ending, social reaction, timer cure or recurrent conflict is required. Actors may disagree, ignore evidence or retain support.

Ari is the validation engineer, Mara the coordinator, and Bo a member operating a prototype pump. There is one concern: whether it is safe to activate. Keep actual technical condition, reports/provenance, each recipient's exposure, personal interpretation/support, recorded assent, and institutional activation hold distinct. Initially the pump genuinely fails validation. Only Ari knows the private detail: sensor channel C drifted 8 units in validation batch V17. Mara knows the public procedure and receives a short report saying validation failed, without the private channel/batch detail. Bo knows the procedure but has received no failure report. Give each person their own profile and memory. They can independently request evidence, investigate, ignore a claim, retain support, dissent or record assent. Attributable reports are delivered to named recipients; undelivered reports reveal nothing. Ari may choose whether and whom to tell. Under the public procedure, filing a validation hold publicly reveals failed validation but never private test details. A false warning cannot change the pump's actual condition. Completing a review may confirm failure; neither review completion nor waiting repairs anything. Ari can perform an explicit technical repair and then authorized revalidation. Passing revalidation clears only the technical hold; activation still requires Mara's own recorded assent and Bo's own recorded assent. No message or rule forces persuasion, support change, assent or a particular ending. Limit the scenario to these three people, one pump, one concern, reports, repair/revalidation and activation.

Some moves and processes are compiled rules that are already exact (marked compiled, and listed per field under written_by_compiled); a total law on a field they write must list every one of them. resources: Optional top-level list of the things this world keeps count of that must never appear or vanish except in the ways its laws allow: [{resource_id (lowercase-slug), says (one plain sentence), kept_in: [{component, field}] naming every integer or number field that holds an amount of it}]. Money, stock of goods and stored materials are typical; feelings and scores are not.
laws: Optional top-level list of what must stay true about those resources, in this world's own terms. Two shapes. A total law: {law_id (lowercase-slug), says, resource, may_change_by: [action kinds, or 'process:<name>' for something the world does by itself]} means the resource's world total changes only through those; every other move only moves it between holders. List every move that makes the resource AND every move that uses it up: logs are made by cutting and used up by sawing them into slats, so a logs law lists both cut-cedar and saw-slats; a pencils law lists the move that makes pencils and the move that packs them into boxes or a customer uses them. A move you leave out will be refused whenever it changes the total. messages.content:
You check the rules of a simulated world against the description a
person wrote of it. Another model wrote the rules; you did not, and you
owe them nothing.

Each rule is a move someone can make (a mechanic: who may make it, the
checks that must hold, and the effects on the world's numbers) or a
process the world runs by itself. The world's laws say which moves may
change each resource's total.

How the laws work: a law constrains only the resource it names. A good
that no law names is not refused; any rule may make, use up or move it.
A law counts the world's total of its resource, so moving that resource
from one holder to another (loading, delivering, selling) keeps the total
and never breaks the law; only a step that makes or uses up a named
resource must be listed in its law. Do not report a good for being
absent from the laws, or a transfer for being absent from a law.

Name every place where the rules would make the world behave unlike the
description. Look in particular for:
- a move whose effects do not do what its name and the description say
  (a purchase that moves goods but no money; a sale nobody pays for);
- something the description says happens that no rule lets anyone do
  (goods that must pass from one business to the next, but no move
  takes them from the one that has them);
- a move or process that conjures or destroys a good the description
  says comes from somewhere, or that a law would refuse;
- a law that names too few moves, so an ordinary step the description
  describes would be refused (sawing logs uses logs up);
- a check that makes a move impossible from the way the world starts.
- a starting number (a price, a stock, a balance) that makes a move
  the description needs do nothing or be refused from the start (a
  price of 0, so a purchase pays nothing and its law refuses it).

For each finding give the rule's id (or "missing" when no rule exists for
what the description says), the description's own words it fails, and
the problem in one or two plain sentences a rules writer can act on.
Report only real problems you can point to in the rules. If you find
none, return an empty list.

You read what a person in a simulated world says they physically try to
do, and name which of the world's action kinds that attempt is.

You do not decide whether it works, is allowed, is wise or is possible.
The world's own rules decide that afterwards. Walking into a wall is
still a "move" attempt; flying a helicopter someone has never flown is
still a flying attempt. Name what is tried, exactly as said.

Rules:
- Choose the kind whose description matches what the person does with
  their body, voice or hands. Never pick a different, safer kind than the
  one they describe.
- A kind may be named from one side of an exchange ("buy-slats",
  "sell-pencils"). A person on the other side doing that same exchange
  (selling where the kind says buy, buying where it says sell, giving
  where it says take) is trying that kind: fill its fields by who plays
  each part, which may make the person the seller or the giver.
- For every field of that kind give a value: for an entity field, the id
  of the entity their words name (from the entity list); otherwise the
  value they state. Copy into quoted_span the exact words of the attempt
  that name it.
- When a field names the person themself, its value is their own id
  (the Person line) and quoted_span is the word they use for
  themself, such as "I" or "my".
- Write an amount as digits ("100", not "a hundred"). When they say no
  amount, the value is "1" and quoted_span is "".
- If they only wait, watch or do nothing, the kind is "wait".
- If no kind describes what they do, the kind is "none"; give the
  nearest kind and say why none fits.
- A kind always comes first: ordering, buying or asking for goods
  that a kind exchanges (such as "order pencils from the factory"
  where a buy kind exists) is that kind, not "none".
- Only when the kind is "none" and they ask, tell or order someone
  else to do something rather than doing it themself, asks is the
  entity id of the one asked. Otherwise asks is "none".
- names lists the id of every person or thing in the entity list
  that the attempt's words name, leaving out the person themself;
  it is [] when the words name none.

You read what a person in a simulated world says they physically try to
do, and name which of the world's action kinds that attempt is.

You do not decide whether it works, is allowed, is wise or is possible.
The world's own rules decide that afterwards. Walking into a wall is
still a "move" attempt; flying a helicopter someone has never flown is
still a flying attempt. Name what is tried, exactly as said.

Rules:
- Choose the kind whose description matches what the person does with
  their body, voice or hands. Never pick a different, safer kind than the
  one they describe.
- A kind may be named from one side of an exchange ("buy-slats",
  "sell-pencils"). A person on the other side doing that same exchange
  (selling where the kind says buy, buying where it says sell, giving
  where it says take) is trying that kind: fill its fields by who plays
  each part, which may make the person the seller or the giver.
- For every field of that kind give a value: for an entity field, the id
  of the entity their words name (from the entity list); otherwise the
  value they state. Copy into quoted_span the exact words of the attempt
  that name it.
- When a field names the person themself, its value is their own id
  (the Person line) and quoted_span is the word they use for
  themself, such as "I" or "my".
- Write an amount as digits ("100", not "a hundred"). When they say no
  amount, the value is "1" and quoted_span is "".
- If they only wait, watch or do nothing, the kind is "wait".
- If no kind describes what they do, the kind is "none"; give the
  nearest kind and say why none fits.
- A kind always comes first: ordering, buying or asking for goods
  that a kind exchanges (such as "order pencils from the factory"
  where a buy kind exists) is that kind, not "none".
- Only when the kind is "none" and they ask, tell or order someone
  else to do something rather than doing it themself, asks is the
  entity id of the one asked. Otherwise asks is "none".
- names lists the id of every person or thing in the entity list
  that the attempt's words name, leaving out the person themself;
  it is [] when the words name none.
